HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded answer): In this survey of 276 practitioners on requirements engineering for ML-enabled systems (194 answered the documentation question), the two least-used documentation formats are **BDD scenarios** and the **ML Canvas**. Only 4/194 respondents (2.06%, 95% respondent-level bootstrap percentile CI [0.52%, 4.12%]; BCa identical) indicate their organization uses BDD scenarios, and 15/194 (7.73%, 95% CI [4.12%, 11.86%]) indicate using the ML Canvas — far below every other named format (vision documents and goal models 14.9%, data models 17.5%, use case models 19.6%, prototypes 21.6%, requirements lists 26.3%, user stories 32.5%, notebooks 34.0%). The free-text "Others" catch-all ties ML Canvas at 15/194 but is not a named format and is reported separately; 15.5% of respondents (30/194) report not documenting ML aspects at all. The ranking is robust across all operationalizations tested (276-row denominator: 1.45% and 5.43%; completed-only n=164: 2.44% and 8.54%; documenting-respondents-only n=146: 2.74% and 10.27%; share-of-total-mentions: 0.96% and 3.61%).

TRANSPARENT DISCREPANCY NOTE (as instructed): The figures quoted in the question — 10.13% (95% CI [9.926, 10.333]) and 4.366% (95% CI [4.231, 4.501]) — could NOT be reproduced from this CSV by any systematic variant tested: (i) per-format 'quoted' rates over the 194 valid respondents, all 276 rows (−77 as non-use), completed-only (164), sentinel-cleaned (225/190), and documenting-only (146) subsets; (ii) share-of-total-mentions with 416/386/371 denominators; (iii) inverted 'quoted'/'not quoted' coding; (iv) weighted variants (experience, projects, duration). The only numerically compatible combinations are hypothetical integer pairs such as 28/276 and 12/276 or 30/296 and 13/296 — but the Q10 block contains no counts of 28, 12, or 13 (observed counts: 4, 15, 15, 29, 29, 30, 34, 38, 42, 51, 63, 66), so no variant realizes them. Moreover, the stated CI half-widths (±0.204 pp and ±0.135 pp) are mutually consistent with a binomial proportion but imply an effective sample size of ≈84,000–88,000 observations — impossible for n ≤ 276, where any respondent-level bootstrap CI must be roughly an order of magnitude wider (e.g., ±1.8 pp for BDD scenarios at n=194). The quoted percentages/CIs therefore most plausibly derive from a different (e.g., original-study) version of the data; the qualitative conclusion above — BDD scenarios least used, ML Canvas second least — is what this CSV supports.

payload.hypothesis: The two least-used documentation formats for requirements in ML-enabled system projects are BDD scenarios (4/194 = 2.06%, 95% bootstrap CI [0.52%, 4.12%]) and the ML Canvas (15/194 = 7.73%, 95% CI [4.12%, 11.86%]); the free-text 'Others' catch-all ties ML Canvas but is not a named format. The percentages quoted in the question (10.13% CI [9.926,10.333]; 4.366% CI [4.231,4.501]) could not be reproduced from this CSV under any tested denominator/definition variant, and their CI widths imply an effective sample of ~85,000, impossible for n<=276; the qualitative finding (BDD scenarios least, ML Canvas second least) is robust across all operationalizations tested.
payload.workflow: Loaded the CSV (276x202); identified the Q10_ML_Documentation_* block as a 12-option multi-select encoded 'quoted'/'not quoted' with -77 = question skipped by 82 respondents (194 valid); operationalized 'used' as 'quoted' among valid respondents; computed per-format usage rates; ranked the 10 named formats (Others and Not_Documented reported separately); respondent-level bootstrap resampling of the 194 valid rows, B=10,000, seed 2024, 95% percentile CI plus BCa robustness; sensitivity analyses over the 276-row denominator, completed-only, documenting-only and share-of-mentions bases; systematic reconciliation pass over integer-count pairs, subsets, alternative codings and weightings showing the quoted figures/CIs are not reproducible from this CSV.
